Etymology: Pictogram (象形) – the sun. A dot or line was added in the centre to distinguish it from visually similar characters, e.g. 口 (kǒu). Compare earlier forms of the character with the astronomical and astrological symbol for the Sun (☉) and the Egyptian hieroglyph 𓇳. From Proto-Sino-Tibetan *ku-ni(k). Cognate to Tibetan ཉི་མ (nyi ma, “sun, day”), Burmese နေ (ne, “sun”) or Burmese နေ့ (ne., “day”), S'gaw Karen နံၤ (nĩ, “day”), and Nuosu ꑍ (nyip, “day, daytime”).   1. (dialectal Mandarin, dialectal Jin, dialectal Wu, dialectal Xiang, vulgar, often in abuses) to fuck; to have sexual intercourse with Tags: Jin, Mandarin, Wu, Xiang, dialectal, often, vulgar
    Sense id: en-日-zh-character-TLvHXmzG Categories (other): Chinese links with redundant alt parameters, Chinese links with redundant wikilinks, Jin Chinese, Mandarin Chinese, Wu Chinese, Xiang Chinese
  2. (dialectal Mandarin, Jin) Prefix in certain verbs or adjectives with a negative connotation. Tags: Jin, Mandarin, dialectal
    Sense id: en-日-zh-character--vnrRVMB Categories (other): Jin Chinese, Mandarin Chinese, Chinese links with manual fragments Disambiguation of Chinese links with manual fragments: 32 68

Etymology: Possibly due to assimilation of 金 (kim) and 日 (nyit). Note that 金 ends with /m/ in Old and Middle Chinese. Etymology templates: {{glossary|assimilation}} assimilation Head templates: {{head|zh|hanzi}} 日
  1. Only used in 日磾 /日䃅, a Han dynasty-era personal name borne by Jin Midi (金日磾) and Ma Midi (馬日磾).

  "etymology_text": "Pictogram (象形) – the sun. A dot or line was added in the centre to distinguish it from visually similar characters, e.g. 口 (kǒu). Compare earlier forms of the character with the astronomical and astrological symbol for the Sun (☉) and the Egyptian hieroglyph 𓇳.\nFrom Proto-Sino-Tibetan *ku-ni(k). Cognate to Tibetan ཉི་མ (nyi ma, “sun, day”), Burmese နေ (ne, “sun”) or Burmese နေ့ (ne., “day”), S'gaw Karen နံၤ (nĩ, “day”), and Nuosu ꑍ (nyip, “day, daytime”).",

  "etymology_text": "Pictogram (象形) – the sun. A dot or line was added in the centre to distinguish it from visually similar characters, e.g. 口 (kǒu). Compare earlier forms of the character with the astronomical and astrological symbol for the Sun (☉) and the Egyptian hieroglyph 𓇳.\nFrom Proto-Sino-Tibetan *ku-ni(k). Cognate to Tibetan ཉི་མ (nyi ma, “sun, day”), Burmese နေ (ne, “sun”) or Burmese နေ့ (ne., “day”), S'gaw Karen နံၤ (nĩ, “day”), and Nuosu ꑍ (nyip, “day, daytime”).",
